:::{#thm-lu-solve}
#### Solving a system with an LU factorization

If $\matr{A} = \matr{L} \matr{U}$ is an LU factorization (@def-lu)
and the diagonal entries of $\matr{U}$ are all nonzero,
then for every $\vecf{b} \in \reals^n$ the system $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$
has exactly one solution:
solve $\matr{L} \vecf{y} = \vecf{b}$ by forward substitution,
then $\matr{U} \vecf{x} = \vecf{y}$ by back substitution (@thm-back-substitution).

:::

::: proof

$\matr{L}$ has diagonal entries $1$ and $\matr{U}$ has nonzero ones,
so each of the two triangular systems has exactly one solution (@thm-back-substitution).
If $\vecf{y}$ and $\vecf{x}$ are those solutions, then
$\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \matr{L}\,(\matr{U} \vecf{x}) = \matr{L} \vecf{y} = \vecf{b}$ (@thm-matmul-assoc),
so $\vecf{x}$ is a solution.
Conversely, if $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$, then $\vecf{y} \eqdef \matr{U} \vecf{x}$
satisfies $\matr{L} \vecf{y} = \matr{L}\,(\matr{U} \vecf{x}) = (\matr{L} \matr{U})\,\vecf{x} = \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$
(@thm-matmul-assoc),
so $\vecf{y}$ is the unique solution of that system,
and $\vecf{x}$ is then the unique solution of $\matr{U} \vecf{x} = \vecf{y}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-lu-solve}
#### Two triangular solves

With $\matr{L}$ and $\matr{U}$ of @exm-lu, solve $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (8, -11, -3)$.
Forward substitution on $\matr{L} \vecf{y} = (8, -11, -3)$ gives
$y_1 = 8$,
$y_2 = -11 + \tfrac{3}{2} \cd 8 = 1$,
$y_3 = -3 + 8 - 4 \cd 1 = 1$.
Back substitution on $\matr{U} \vecf{x} = (8, 1, 1)$ is @exm-back-substitution,
which gives $\vecf{x} = (2, 3, -1)$.
As a check, $\matr{A}\,(2, 3, -1) = (4 + 3 + 1,\; -6 - 3 - 2,\; -4 + 3 - 2) = (8, -11, -3)$.

:::
